notes: Prefix/suffix-sum plus dp, too much for a Monday.
aiExplanation: This function counts, for every remainder `r` from `0` to `k-1`, how many **contiguous subarrays** of `nums` have a product whose remainder modulo `k` equals `r`. It uses a **rolling dynamic-programming array** called `dp`, where `dp[r]` holds the number of subarrays *ending at the current position* whose product leaves remainder `r`. For each new element `nums[i]`, a fresh array `ndp` is built: first the single-element subarray `[nums[i]]` is counted by incrementing `ndp[nums[i] % k]`, and then every subarray that ended at the previous position with remainder `r` is extended by one element, so its new remainder becomes `(r * nums[i]) % k` and its count `dp[r]` is added there. Since only remainders matter (a product mod `k` depends only on the previous remainder mod `k`), the array never needs to store real products. After each step `dp` is replaced by `ndp`, and the counts are **accumulated into `result`**, so by the end `result[r]` totals all subarrays across every ending position with remainder `r`. This runs in `O(n * k)` time and `O(k)` extra space.
